exercises.video_explanation_script: The RDL is the king of hamstring exercises. Start standing tall with the bar at your hips. From here, push your hips back like you're trying to close a car door behind you. Keep your spine neutral and the bar close to your legs as you lower down. You should feel a deep stretch in your hamstrings. Only go as low as you can while keeping your back flat - typically mid-shin level. Then drive your hips forward to stand back up, squeezing your glutes at the top. This isn't a squat - your knees stay at roughly the same angle the whole time. The movement comes from your hips. The RDL is essential for building strong, powerful hamstrings.

exercises.video_explanation_script: The lying leg curl is a staple hamstring exercise. Lie face down on the machine with the pad resting on your lower calves, just above your heels. Make sure your knees align with the machine's pivot point. From here, curl your heels up toward your glutes by bending your knees. Really squeeze your hamstrings at the top. The critical thing is to keep your hips pressed flat against the pad throughout - don't let them lift up. Then control the weight back down to full extension. This exercise isolates the hamstrings through knee flexion, which is essential because hamstrings do more than just hip extension. The lying leg curl is perfect for building hamstring size and strength.

exercises.video_explanation_script: The seated leg curl is an excellent variation for hamstring development. Sit in the machine with your back flat against the pad and the lower pad positioned against your lower calves. Secure the thigh pad over your quads. From this extended position, curl your lower legs back underneath you by bending your knees. Think about driving your heels toward the floor behind you. Squeeze your hamstrings hard when your legs are fully curled. Then extend your legs back out with control. The key is keeping your back pressed against the pad throughout. The seated position uniquely emphasizes the short head of the biceps femoris, which is why it's a great complement to other hamstring exercises.

exercises.video_explanation_script: The Nordic hamstring curl is one of the most effective exercises for building bulletproof hamstrings. Kneel on a pad with your ankles secured by a partner or under a fixed object. Start in a tall kneeling position with your body forming a straight line from your knees to your head. From here, slowly lower your body forward while keeping your hips extended. Your hamstrings should be fighting to control the descent the entire way down. Lower as far as you can control, then catch yourself with your hands and push off the ground to return to the starting position. Most people can't pull themselves back up initially - that's completely normal. The eccentric phase is where the real magic happens. Nordic curls are phenomenal for building hamstring strength and preventing injuries.

exercises.video_explanation_script: The good morning is a classic posterior chain exercise. Set up with a barbell on your back like you would for a squat, but use lighter weight. Stand with feet hip to shoulder-width apart with a slight bend in your knees. From here, push your hips back and hinge forward at your hips while keeping your spine completely neutral. Your knees should barely move - they maintain that slight bend throughout. Hinge forward until your torso is near parallel to the ground or as far as you can go while keeping your back flat. You should feel a deep stretch in your hamstrings. Then drive your hips forward to stand back up tall. The key is maintaining that neutral spine throughout - never round your back. Good mornings are excellent for building a strong posterior chain.

exercises.video_explanation_script: The glute ham raise is one of the most complete hamstring exercises you can do. Position yourself in the GHR machine with your ankles secured and knees on the pad. Start with your body in a straight line parallel to the ground. From here, lower your body forward by extending your knees, keeping your entire body rigid - don't break at the hips. Control the descent with your hamstrings. Then pull yourself back up by flexing your knees and engaging your hamstrings and glutes. Drive your toes down into the ankle pad. The GHR combines both functions of the hamstrings - knee flexion and hip extension - making it incredibly effective. Most people need assistance when starting out, and that's completely normal. This exercise builds bulletproof hamstrings.

exercises.video_explanation_script: The single-leg RDL is one of the most challenging and rewarding exercises for your hamstrings and balance. Stand on one leg with a slight bend in your knee. From here, push your hips back as you hinge forward, extending your free leg behind you. Think of your torso and back leg as one unit - they move together. Keep your hips square to the ground; don't let them open up. Lower down until your torso is about parallel to the ground, feeling a deep stretch in your hamstring. Then drive through your heel to return to standing, squeezing your hamstring and glute at the top. This exercise builds unilateral strength, improves balance, and addresses any imbalances between legs.

exercises.video_explanation_script: The standing leg curl is a great unilateral variation for hamstring development. Stand in the machine on one leg with the pad positioned against your lower calf on your working leg. Hold the handles for support. From this extended position, curl your heel up toward your glute by bending your knee. Keep your hips completely still - don't rotate or swing. Squeeze your hamstring hard at the top. Then control the weight back down to full extension. The key is keeping your body stable throughout - all the movement should come from your knee flexing. This single-leg variation is excellent for identifying and fixing any imbalances between your legs.

exercises.video_explanation_script: The Swiss ball hamstring curl is an excellent bodyweight exercise for building strong hamstrings. Lie on your back with your heels on top of a stability ball and your arms at your sides. Start by lifting your hips off the ground, forming a straight line from your shoulders to your heels. From this elevated position, pull the ball toward you by bending your knees and curling with your heels. Your hips should stay up the entire time - don't let them drop. Pull the ball in as close as you can, squeezing your hamstrings and glutes. Then control the ball as you extend your legs back out. The instability of the ball adds a great challenge and forces your hamstrings to work hard throughout the entire range.

exercises.video_explanation_script: The stiff-leg deadlift is an advanced hamstring exercise that creates an incredible stretch. The key difference from an RDL is that your legs stay nearly straight - just a micro-bend in the knees. Start standing tall with the barbell at your hips. Push your hips back as you lower the bar down the front of your legs. Keep your legs almost completely straight. You should feel an intense stretch in your hamstrings, especially where they connect to your glutes. Only go as low as you can while maintaining a flat back - typically mid-shin or below. Then drive your hips forward to stand back up. This exercise requires good hamstring flexibility and should be loaded lighter than an RDL. The increased range and reduced knee bend make it exceptional for hamstring development.

exercises.video_explanation_script: The razor curl is an extremely advanced hamstring exercise focusing on eccentric strength. Kneel with your ankles secured under a loaded barbell or held by a partner. Start in a tall kneeling position. From here, slowly extend your knees, lowering your body toward the ground. The key is to resist this descent with your hamstrings for as long as possible - fight every inch of the way down. Your hamstrings are trying to stop your knees from straightening. Lower as slowly as you can control, then catch yourself with your hands when you can't resist anymore. Return to kneeling and repeat. This exercise creates extreme hamstring soreness, so start with very low volume - maybe just 3-5 reps total. It's incredibly effective but must be progressed very carefully.

exercises.video_explanation_script: The kettlebell swing is a powerful exercise for building explosive hip strength and conditioning. Set up with the kettlebell on the ground in front of you, feet about shoulder-width apart. Hinge forward and grip the kettlebell with both hands. From here, hike the kettlebell back between your legs like snapping a football. Then explosively drive your hips forward, snapping them through to standing. The kettlebell should float up to about chest or shoulder height - your arms are just along for the ride. At the top, you should be standing completely upright with your glutes squeezed hard. Let the kettlebell fall back down and hinge your hips to absorb it. This is all about explosive hip power. The swing builds powerful hamstrings and glutes while also providing an amazing conditioning workout.
